hints: Focus on gas volumes at the same T and P, remember equal volumes mean equal moles so volume ratios are mole ratios.
Compare 10 cm3 of J with 20 cm3 of CO2 to work out how many carbon atoms must be in one molecule of J.
Now do the same nitrogen balance using 10 cm3 of J giving 5 cm3 of N2, remembering each N2 has two N atoms.
walkthrough:
**Use Avogadro's principle**

All volumes are measured at the same T and P, so volume ratio = moles ratio. Think in terms of reacting volumes.

$$10 \text{ volumes J} \rightarrow 20 \text{ volumes CO}_2 + 5 \text{ volumes N}_2 + \text{ steam}$$

**Balance carbon atoms**

10 cm3 of J produces 20 cm3 of CO2. That is a 1 to 2 ratio.

Each $\text{CO}_2$ contains 1 C, so 2 molecules of $\text{CO}_2$ contain 2 C atoms. Therefore 1 molecule of J must contain 2 C atoms.

$$\text{C atoms in J} = \frac{20}{10} \times 1 = 2$$

**Balance nitrogen atoms**

10 cm3 of J produces 5 cm3 of $\text{N}_2$. That is a 2 to 1 ratio.

Each $\text{N}_2$ contains 2 N atoms, so be careful to count atoms, not molecules.

$$\text{N atoms in J} = \frac{5}{10} \times 2 = 1$$

**Test the three formulae**

J must be $\text{C}_2$ with one N. Statement 1 is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$ with two N atoms, so it would give twice as much $\text{N}_2$. Statements 2 and 3 both have $\text{C}_2$ and one N, so both fit the C and N data. The volume of steam is not given, so H cannot be checked.

Hence only 2 and 3 are possible.

options.A: Incorrect. This option means 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. Statement 1 is impossible because $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$ has 2 N atoms per molecule and would give 10 cm3 of $\text{N}_2$ from 10 cm3 of J, not 5 cm3.
options.B: Incorrect. This option means 1 and 2 only are possible. Statement 1 fails the nitrogen balance as above, while statement 3 is actually possible and is wrongly excluded.
options.C: Correct. Both $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{N}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_7\text{N}$ contain 2 C and 1 N, matching 20 cm3 $\text{CO}_2$ and 5 cm3 $\text{N}_2$ from 10 cm3 J. Hydrogen cannot be distinguished without the steam volume.
options.D: Incorrect. This option means 1 only is possible. Statement 1 is the one statement that is definitely wrong because its $\text{N}_2$ volume would be double the observed value.
